entities.summary: William Neville, Earl of Kent, KG, jure uxoris 6th Baron Fauconberg, was a pivotal English nobleman and soldier who played a crucial role in the Wars of the Roses. His strategic alliances and military victories significantly impacted the fate of the Plantagenet dynasty and the course of English history. As a key figure in the medieval period, Neville's legacy extends to the modern era through his descendants, who continue to shape the British nobility. His biography serves as a testament to the enduring influence of medieval knights and the complexities of royal politics. The 1463 assassination of Neville marked the end of an era, as the Plantagenet claim to the throne was finally extinguished, paving the way for the Tudor dynasty.
